title: Interop Oracle: Golden Prompt & Contract Suite for Streaming, Tools, and Structured Output
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an authoritative conformance and regression harness (the 'Interop Oracle') that validates API compatibility across streaming, tool/function calling, and structured output features using a curated golden prompt corpus. The suite will run in CI, surface regressions via dashboards and PR annotations, and provide deterministic fingerprints for canonical prompt-response pairs.

Scope:
- Golden prompt corpus for streaming + tool call scenarios (happy path, edge path, backpressure, partial tool failures).
- Contract tests verifying: streaming chunking semantics, event ordering, content integrity with function/tool call payloads, and structured-output JSON schema stability.
- CI integration: matrix runs for SDK versions (js/python/go), server runtime variants (hosted, dedicated emulation), and quantization profiles that affect decoding.
- Oracle: deterministic matching using fuzzy token-level metrics + canonicalization rules (timestamp/nonce normalization) with configurable thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
1) CI job "interop-oracle/regressions" executes on PRs that touch runtime, SDK, or API surface and reports pass/fail with annotated diffs.
2) Golden corpus stored in repo under /testdata/golden/ with metadata manifest (prompt id, expected event stream, normalized response).
3) False-positive rate under 1% during a 2-week rolling window on main branch.
4) Clear remediation playbook in Confluence and a dashboard showing historical regressions and flaky tests.

Out of scope: fuzz-driven generative tests that do not map to a golden prompt; these will be tracked separately.
risks: Test flakiness due to non-deterministic sampling/temperature settings
Large golden corpus size causing CI timeouts
Ambiguity in canonicalization rules for structured outputs
decision_log: 2026-02-18: Picked token-level normalized Levenshtein + embedding cosine as primary regression signal (balance of strictness and tolerance).
2026-02-22: Will canonicalize timestamps/UUIDs and redact client-side ephemeral fields before comparison.
2026-02-28: CI to run a fast smoke set on PR and full regression nightly; PR runs will gate only on critical scenarios to reduce latency.
implementation_notes: Runner implemented as a Go micro-binary (tests/oracle-runner) to reduce cross-language CI friction; uses SDK bindings to exercise streaming and tool-call APIs. Golden fixtures include both .ndjson event streams and explicit JSON-schema for structured outputs. Comparison pipeline: normalize -> tokenize -> compare -> compute signal -> store result artifact. Artifacts uploaded to S3 and linked from GitHub Actions job output.
ci_configuration: GitHub Actions workflow: .github/workflows/interop-oracle.yml. Jobs: smoke-pr (fast suite), nightly-full (full corpus), canary-on-staging (against staging runtime). Matrix axes: sdk=[js,python,go], runtime_variant=[hosted-sim,dedicated-sim], quant=[fp16,int8]. PR annotations use the GitHub Checks API; failures include a diff artifact and a link to the failing golden ID.

test_plan_summary: 1) Unit tests for canonicalization and comparison functions. 2) Integration tests that run golden prompts through SDK stubs in CI. 3) Manual verification for first 50 golden cases with runtime and SDK owners to validate baseline. 4) Nightly full-corpus run with alerting on failures above threshold.
expected_outcome: Reduce production regressions in streaming/tool/structured-output surface by catching API-compatibility changes earlier in CI, provide deterministic artifacts for incident triage, and enable confident runtime refactors with low operational risk.
